title: The Value of AI 2026
gist: A 2026 SAP and Oxford Economics survey of 2,600 senior executives across 13 countries finds enterprises accelerating AI adoption and investment, with ROI still growing as AI gets embedded in core business operations. The stated gating factors on realising further value are data readiness, governance, workforce transformation and responsible scaling.

themes.theme: Enterprise AI adoption and measured ROI

insights.claim: A 2026 survey of 2,600 senior executives across 13 countries, run by SAP and Oxford Economics, finds that businesses are accelerating both AI adoption and AI investment.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: A large multi-country executive panel is a usable proxy for enterprise software demand; a corroborating read on whether AI budgets are still expanding rather than consolidating.
insights.quote: A new study by SAP and Oxford Economics surveys 2,600 senior executives across 13 countries, assessing organisations’ progress towards all things AI.
insights.locator: A new study by SAP and Oxford

insights.claim: Return on investment from corporate AI deployments is reported as continuing to grow as AI becomes embedded across core business operations rather than confined to pilots.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: If ROI improves with depth of embedding rather than plateauing, spend on enterprise application and data-platform vendors is more durable than a pilot-cycle bubble; watch for the report's actual ROI figures on release.
insights.quote: businesses are accelerating AI adoption and investment, with ROI continuing to grow as AI becomes embedded across core business operations
insights.locator: The 2026 SAP and Oxford Economics research

insights.claim: The research frames its central purpose as quantifying the tangible, measurable value of AI adoption across organisations rather than describing capability or intent.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Signals that the enterprise AI narrative has moved from adoption counts to value quantification — the metric buyers and investors will increasingly be held to.
insights.quote: attempts to quantify the tangible value of AI adoption across organisations
insights.locator: The 2026 SAP and Oxford Economics research attempts

insights.claim: Four specific bottlenecks are identified as what organisations must address to fully realise AI's value: data readiness, governance, workforce transformation and responsible scaling.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Points spend toward data infrastructure, governance tooling and change-management services as the adjacent beneficiaries of AI budgets, not just model vendors.
insights.quote: businesses are looking to address critical challenges around data readiness, governance, workforce transformation and responsible scaling.

themes.theme: Provenance and reliability of the research

insights.claim: The study is a vendor-partnered consulting report produced by Oxford Economics' Thought Leadership team in partnership with SAP, an interested party in enterprise AI software.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Sponsored thought leadership tends to skew optimistic on ROI; treat the headline value claims as directional and cross-check against independent enterprise AI spend data.

insights.claim: Data capture and survey analysis for the programme sit with an Oxford Economics team led by Jamie Snowdon, a former PAC, IDC and HFS Research analyst with over 25 years in IT and business services research.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Methodology is run by IT-market research veterans, which raises the credibility of the sizing and survey analysis even in a sponsored report.
insights.quote: Jamie Snowdon oversees data capture and analysis for Oxford Economics’ Thought Leadership group.
insights.locator: Jamie Snowdon oversees data capture and analysis
